question.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $B$ to the basis $C$ is given by 
${P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}].$
Find the change-of-coordinates matrix from $C$ to $B$  .

current_example.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $\mathcal{B}$ to the basis $\mathcal{C}$ is given by 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275083/assets/95381e0c5c4ea467686b9b2e9b6fc80563dae1d7b76f4a102c0e988919fde9bc.svg)
Find the change-of-coordinates matrix from $\mathcal{C}$ to $\mathcal{B}.$
current_example.worked_solution:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $\mathcal{C}$ to $\mathcal{B}$ is the inverse of the change-of-coordinates matrix from $\mathcal{B}$ to $\mathcal{C}.$ Therefore, we simply need to find the inverse of the given matrix.

Computing the inverse of $P_{\small\mathcal{B}\to\mathcal{C}},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}-4 & -6 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-4)\cdot 5-(-6)\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}5 & 6 \\ -3 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =(-\frac{1}{2})\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 & 6 \\ -3 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{2} & -3 \\ \frac{3}{2} & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
